sections.h2: What makes selling a house in Kirkwood, MO unusual?
sections.html:
Kirkwood requires an occupancy permit and inspection from sellers of residential property. Put it on your calendar before photos or pricing talks.

Kirkwood is an inner-ring suburb in western St. Louis County and has called itself home rule since 1984. It was platted in 1852, the railroad arrived in 1853, and it is often described as the first planned suburb west of the Mississippi. The city is named for James P. Kirkwood, chief engineer of the Pacific Railroad. The original plat banned industry, which helps explain why the city still reads as a leafy residential grid around a train station.

sections.h2: How do the Census numbers set Kirkwood apart from other Missouri cities?
sections.html:
Kirkwood is a small, settled, high-value market. Census figures for July 2025 show 29,331 people, half a percent fewer than the 29,465 in the April 2020 base, packed into only 9.18 square miles of land. About 77 percent of homes are owner occupied, and 91.2 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier.

  • Middle home value among owners (2020 to 2024): $451,400
  • Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage: $2,414
  • Median gross rent: $1,348
  • Median household income: $121,270
  • Adults with a bachelor's degree or higher: 67.9 percent

Compare that median value with $168,300 in Joplin and $242,900 in Kansas City. At Kirkwood prices a repair list matters, since every sale must clear the city's occupancy inspection.

sections.h2: What is the occupancy permit and how do I get one in Kirkwood?
sections.html:
Under the Building Division's rules, every change in occupancy needs a permit that includes an inspection, and sellers and landlords of residential and commercial property are the people who apply. Single family houses and duplexes use the Residential Occupancy permit, while condos and apartments use the Multi-Family version. Call 314-822-5823 on weekdays between 8:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. with questions.

Kirkwood occupancy steps for a sale (source: kirkwoodmo.org Building Division)
StepWhoWhat happens
1SellerRegister on the Kirkwood Public Portal and apply for the occupancy permit
2SellerOnce the permit is approved, paid and issued, request the inspection online or by phone
3BuyerAfter the property passes, the new occupant gets an Occupancy Certificate
4BuyerShow the certificate to Kirkwood finance to transfer utilities and to register children with the school district

The Building Division office is on the lower level of City Hall at 139 S Kirkwood Rd, 63122. If the house passes, a buyer does not need a fresh permit. Any problems found have to be corrected before the property passes.

sections.h2: Which codes and permits matter if I repair the house first?
sections.html:
Kirkwood adopted the 2021 International codes effective April 1, 2026, replacing the 2015 set. Permits cover residential and commercial construction, remodeling and repairs, demolition, fences and decks, swimming pools, retaining walls, plumbing, electrical and mechanical work, and sewer lateral applications. Contractors need a Kirkwood business license, which is managed through the same portal, and plans larger than 11 by 17 inches go in digitally.

Projects that touch the exterior may need review by the Architectural Review Board, the Board of Adjustment, the Landmarks Commission or the Planning and Zoning Commission before a permit issues. In a city with a Historic District and a Landmarks Commission, check with the Building Division before you replace windows, add a deck or alter a front facade.

sections.h2: What costs and timing should I plan around in a Kirkwood sale?
sections.html:
Because Kirkwood prices run high, small percentages become large dollar amounts, and the occupancy inspection adds a step with its own lead time. Work backward from your target closing date and schedule the permit and inspection early.

  • Apply for the occupancy permit on the Kirkwood Public Portal as soon as you decide to sell, since the inspection can only be requested after the permit is approved, paid and issued.
  • Ask the Building Division at 314-822-5823 what the occupancy inspection scope covers, and fix those items before the inspector arrives.
  • Tell your buyer or tenant to complete the Occupancy Certificate form so utilities can move to their name through Kirkwood finance.
  • Record the deed with St. Louis County once the sale funds, and keep the returned original.

Median monthly owner costs in Kirkwood are $2,414 with a mortgage and $849 without one, according to the Census Bureau, so buyers are comparing a purchase against a rent of $1,348 and will push back on anything that looks like deferred maintenance. A buyer who intends to rent the house later will face the same occupancy rules as a landlord, so tell them early.

sections.h2: Which schools, roads and landmarks draw buyers to Kirkwood?
sections.html:
Public education comes from the Kirkwood R-7 School District, which also serves parts of Des Peres, Frontenac, Glendale, Huntleigh, Oakland and Warson Woods. The district has five elementary schools (Tillman, North Glendale, Keysor, Robinson and Westchester), two middle schools (Nipher and North Kirkwood) and Kirkwood High School, established in 1865. Students from Keysor, Westchester and half of Tillman go to North Kirkwood Middle School, and those from North Glendale, Robinson and the other half of Tillman go to Nipher, so the elementary school tells you the middle school.

Interstate 270 runs along the western edge, Interstate 44 touches the southern limit, Manchester Road (Missouri Route 100) borders the north side, and Lindbergh Boulevard (US 61/67) runs through downtown as Kirkwood Road. Kirkwood Station, built in 1893 and listed on the National Register of Historic Places, is the Amtrak Missouri River Runner stop in the St. Louis area outside the central city.

  • Kirkwood Park covers 92 acres south of the town center and includes a lake, trails and an ice arena.
  • The Kirkwood Farmers' Market and The Magic House children's museum draw weekend visitors.
  • The Greentree Festival each September and the Route 66 Cars and Guitars festival on the first Saturday in June bring crowds downtown.

sections.h2: How do I record a deed in St. Louis County after a Kirkwood sale?
sections.html:
Kirkwood lies in St. Louis County, so the deed is filed with its Recorder of Deeds at 41 S Central Ave, Clayton, MO 63105. You can mail or drop off the original notarized document with a check or money order made payable to ROD, and the original comes back within one week of recording. Several third-party vendors also offer e-recording, and they may add their own fees.

The county lists copy prices of $2.00 for the first page and $1.00 for each added page, so a typical printed deed is about $5 plus a convenience fee, with $1 more for each certified copy. A document that meets statute but not formatting standards pays the per-page fee plus a $25 penalty. RSMo 442.380 requires the filing to happen with the recorder of the county where the house stands.

faqs.q: Does a Kirkwood seller need an occupancy inspection?
faqs.a: Yes. Kirkwood's Building Division says sellers of residential and commercial property need an occupancy permit that includes an inspection. Apply through the Kirkwood Public Portal, then request the inspection once the permit is issued.

The new occupant, meaning the buyer or a new tenant. It is issued after the property passes inspection and is needed to transfer utilities through Kirkwood finance and to register children with the Kirkwood School District.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Kirkwood houses?
faqs.a: The Kirkwood R-7 School District. It covers all of Kirkwood and parts of Des Peres, Frontenac, Glendale, Huntleigh, Oakland and Warson Woods, with Kirkwood High School as its single high school.

faqs.q: Where do I record a Kirkwood deed?
faqs.a: At the St. Louis County Recorder of Deeds, 41 S Central Ave, Clayton, MO 63105. You can send the original notarized deed with payment or use an e-recording vendor.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Kirkwood house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes, but the occupancy inspection is a step to plan around. Call the Building Division at 314-822-5823 to learn what the inspection covers, and compare repairing first against selling as-is to a buyer who handles the work.
